messages:
Maya (CS): Heads-up — enterprise client on Dedicated reported rerank results with weird score ranges. Some scores are negative (e.g. -8.2) and a few > 1.0. They think scores should be 0..1.

Maya (CS): Repro payload they sent (redacted):
```json
{
  "query": "best italian restaurants sf",
  "documents": ["docA", "docB", "docC"],
  "top_k": 3
}
```

Maya (CS): No HTTP errors, 200 with JSON. Customer pasted x-request-id: r-ff45a9. They want interpretation and whether this is a bug.

Priya (ML Eng): Quick note — rerank returns raw model scores by default (logits) for the current model variant unless you set normalize=true or use the documented "score_mode". Are they sending anything like "raw_scores" or "score_mode"?

Maya (CS): Good call. Customer says they used SDK v0.9 and just called /v1/rerank with no extra params. I'll ask for full request headers.

Leo (SRE): Also check the model variant. We had a small rollout last week where default score_mode changed from "prob" to "logit" for the cpu-optimized variant. If they're pinned to that variant, they'd see unnormalized negatives.

Aaron (Support): Requested customer to run a quick sanity curl that forces normalized scores:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"best italian restaurants sf","documents":["docA","docB","docC"],"top_k":3,"score_mode":"prob"}'
```

Aaron (Support): Asked them to share output and the x-request-id. If that returns 0..1, we can tell them it's expected behavior for logits.

Priya (ML Eng): If they need stable 0..1 scores for downstream logic, recommend either: 1) request "score_mode":"prob" or "normalize":true; 2) apply softmax on client side; 3) use our rerank-normalized wrapper endpoint. Also mention that negative values are fine for logits — only relative ordering matters.

Maya (CS): Customer replied — curl returned negative values too even with "score_mode":"prob". They pasted the JSON and it still had -0.23, 0.88, -1.1.

Leo (SRE): Hm. If "score_mode":"prob" is ignored that suggests their request might be hitting an older model or an internal mismatch. Can you forward the exact x-request-id? I'll check routing logs and model metadata.

Maya (CS): x-request-id r-ff45a9 from earlier and new one r-ff46d2 from their curl.

Leo (SRE): Found r-ff46d2 in logs — routed to dedicated-pool-11, model redwood-rerank-v2-cpu. That variant still has default logit outputs unless you pass "normalize":true in body (we missed documenting that last week). I filed a small doc patch.

Priya (ML Eng): Confirmed: rerank-v2-cpu returns raw logits by default to save client CPU; normalize flag happens in the serving runtime which we didn't enable by default on that pool. Two options: toggle normalize on request or we can flip the pool config.

Maya (CS): Customer asked for recommended short-term fix and whether their ranking logic is safe.

Priya (ML Eng): Short term: use "score_mode":"prob" OR add "normalize":true in request body. Long term: we'll surface pool defaults in Console and add a note in API docs. Important: when using raw logits, client comparisons are fine for top-K, but thresholds (score > 0.5) are meaningless.

Aaron (Support): Sent repro steps to customer and offered to run a controlled test on their dataset in a dedicated session. Also logged a ticket to Eng Runtime to consider flipping the default for the affected pool or adding a transparent warning header.

rerank-bot: deploy-notice: rollout redwood-rerank-v2-cpu changed config: now supports "normalize_on_request" flag.

Priya (ML Eng): I'll open a quick PR to docs and drop a changelog note. Also adding a sample snippet showing post-processing:
```python
import numpy as np
logits = np.array([ -1.1, -0.23, 0.88])
probs = np.exp(logits) / np.exp(logits).sum()
print(probs)
```

Maya (CS): Customer happy with workaround. They've accepted adding normalize:true for now. Closing loop with them and marking as resolved unless we decide to change pool defaults. :white_check_mark:

Leo (SRE): Follow-up action: ticket INF-4721 to evaluate flipping default for dedicated-pool-11 and add a Console note.

Aaron (Support): I'll add reproduction logs to the ticket and send a short email to the customer about expected semantics and recommended config.

Maya (CS): Thanks team. Good catch on the rollout change, @Priya and @Leo.
